posts.title: Why we jump to conclusions when bad news clusters
posts.description: Thursday afternoon, Microsoft’s email went down. Outlook, Teams, SharePoint and a long list of other services stopped working for people around the world, and it didn’t fully recover until the next day. On Friday, the FAA stopped every flight departure in the United States for over four hours. That same Friday, the National Weather Service reported nationwide internet and communications problems,

posts.title: The ground stop is over, so why is my flight still cancelled?
posts.description: For about ten years, I flew every week. One of the first things you learn when you live out of a suitcase is that your flight isn’t really yours. It’s one link in a chain of aircraft and crews moving around the world, and when something breaks somewhere else in that chain, you feel it.

posts.title: Effective leadership and finding a better way
posts.description: Last week I talked about a situation where a tester had been asked to stop rejecting tickets. In that post, I focused on the beliefs in play. Today, I want to talk about leadership in that same situation.
